clinician.trajectory_summary: A 20-year-old man with a history of right tibial osteosarcoma with brain and lung metastases presented with decreased vision in the right eye. Examination revealed a large pink, nodular, subretinal mass with associated fluid. Ocular ultrasound showed a heterogeneous subretinal mass with medium/high reflectivity and probable necrosis-related air reflectivity. CT scan revealed a heterogeneous well-defined hyperdense uveal mass with contrast enhancement and significant intraocular involvement. MRI showed a well-defined, irregular choroidal mass that was T1-isointense and T2-hypointense. At one-month follow-up, clinical progression included painful eye, retinal detachment, neovascularization, and elevated intraocular pressure treated with topical cycloplegics. Systemic treatment led to a decrease in lesion volume on CT and MRI. The clinical and multimodal imaging findings, along with the systemic osteosarcoma history and tumor response to systemic therapy, support the diagnosis of choroidal metastasis from osteosarcoma.
